messages:
nora: Opened a short PR to clarify rate limit headers and add two tiny SDK examples for Python and JS. Need a quick docs+eng pass: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1163

ben: Can you show the exact header mapping you want in the examples? People keep confusing X-RateLimit-Reset epoch vs client delta.

nora: Added these snippets in the PR body. Python snippet shows computing reset_in_seconds from header; JS shows using server-provided reset_seconds if present.

```python
# Python mapping example
resp = client.complete(prompt)
headers = resp.headers
limit = int(headers.get('X-RateLimit-Limit', 0))
remaining = int(headers.get('X-RateLimit-Remaining', 0))
reset_ts = int(headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
reset_in_seconds = max(0, reset_ts - int(time.time()))
```

kai: Quick note: call out clock skew and recommend using response.json().get('reset_in_seconds') when available. I'll add a one-line comment in the PR.

tess: I updated the console link in the doc from /usage-old to /console/usage and flagged infra for a redirect. Also fixed a tiny typo under "metering" section.

ben: I'll add a minimal unit test in clients/python/tests/test_rate_headers.py asserting remaining decreases after a mock call and reset_in_seconds >= 0. Won't be flaky.
